text.tspan: Elastic Network Interfaces (ENI) and EC2 Hibernate
One AZ (an ENI is bound to its AZ)
EC2 #1 (primary)
EC2 #2 (standby)
eth0 (primary ENI)
eth1 (secondary ENI)
An ENI is a virtual network card. It can have:
• one primary private IPv4, plus secondary ones
• one Elastic IP per private IPv4
• one public IPv4
• one or more security groups
• a MAC address
You can create ENIs on their own and attach or move
them between instances (in the same AZ) for failover:
the private IP moves with the ENI.
Hibernate
stop → the RAM is written to the root EBS volume
start → the RAM is loaded back: processes keep
running, the OS does not reboot (fast start)
Use: long-running processes, apps slow to warm up
Hibernate rules
• root volume must be EBS, ENCRYPTED, and big
enough to hold the RAM
• RAM must be < 150 GB · not for bare metal
• On-Demand, Reserved and Spot instances
• an instance cannot stay hibernated > 60 days
attached now
move on failover
